profile.summary: UTR-LM is a language model for the 5' untranslated region (5' UTR) of mRNA, the stretch before the coding sequence that strongly affects how well an mRNA is translated. It reads a 5' UTR sequence and, after fine-tuning, predicts mean ribosome loading, translation efficiency or mRNA expression level. Pretraining combines masked language modelling with labels computed from the sequence, such as secondary structure and minimum free energy.

summary_quotes.text: Specifically, the 5' UTR, located at the 5' end of an RNA molecule, is a critical determinant of the RNA’s translation efficiency.
We augmented the model with supervised information that can be computed given the sequence, including the secondary structure and minimum free energy, which improved the semantic representation.
The model outperformed the best-known benchmark by up to 42% for predicting the Mean Ribosome Loading, and by up to 60% for predicting the Translation Efficiency and the mRNA Expression Level.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: UTR-LM is built on a modified copy of the ESM-2 transformer code, shipped in the repository. The reported settings are 6 transformer layers, 16 attention heads and an embedding size of 128. Pretraining uses masked language modelling (MLM) and, in the recommended variants, also predicts the minimum free energy (MFE) and/or the secondary structure of the sequence. For downstream tasks the developers fine-tune the whole model and feed the [CLS]-token embedding to a predictor trained with Huber loss.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The repository holds 16 pretrained checkpoint files under Model/Pretrained, named by their pretraining variant (ESM2, ESM2SI, ESM2SS, ESM2SISS, ESM2DSD) and data split, plus 179 checkpoint files under Model/Downstream: 178 for the TE and EL tasks and one for MRL (fold 0 of a single library). The README's own example pretraining command passes --heads 6 --embed_dim 16, which disagrees with the 16 heads and embedding size 128 listed under General Parameters and in the checkpoint file names. A result should name the exact checkpoint file and the repository commit. A runnable copy is also published as a CodeOcean capsule.

run_guide.summary: Set up the UTR-LM environment with its modified ESM code, then fine-tune a pretrained checkpoint for translation efficiency on the Muscle cell line.
prerequisites: Conda, and a CUDA GPU: the commands launch torch.distributed and set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES.
Task data downloaded by hand from the Google Drive folder linked in the README (for the TE and EL task, the Muscle, pc3 or HEK cell-line data).
Paths in the commands changed to your own directories, as the README states.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/a96123155/UTR-LM.git
cd UTR-LM
git checkout --detach b77b589bf182eb9de6a1a5024fa09d44294d94fc
steps.explanation: The README does not give a clone command; this clones the repository named in the README and pins the commit read for this page. Later commands are run from the repository root.
steps.source_locator: README.md: Install step 2 and Instruction Example

quotes.text: In UTRLM environment, install the Python packages listed in the utrlm_requirements.txt file.

steps.title: Create the environment
steps.shell:
conda create -n UTRLM python==3.9.13
conda activate UTRLM
pip install -r utrlm_requirements.txt
steps.explanation: The README's environment steps. The requirements file pins a full conda environment including local build paths, so the plain pip list in the README may be needed instead.

steps.title: Install the modified ESM code
steps.shell:
pip install fair-esm
find -name esm
scp -r ./Scripts/esm ./.conda/envs/UTRLM/lib/python3.9/site-packages/
steps.explanation: Installs fair-esm, then copies the repository's modified esm folder over it. The destination path must match your own environment.

steps.title: Fine-tune for translation efficiency
steps.shell:
cd ./Scripts/UTRLM_downstream
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python3 -m torch.distributed.launch --nproc_per_node=1 --master_port 9001 MJ4_Finetune_extract_append_predictor_CellLine_10fold-lr-huber-DDP.py --device_ids 0 --cell_line Muscle --label_type te_log --seq_type utr --inp_len 100 --huber_loss --modelfile ./Model/ESM2SI_3.1_fiveSpeciesCao_6layers_16heads_128embedsize_4096batchToks_MLMLossMin.pkl --finetune --bos_emb --lr 1e-2 --dropout3 0.2 --epochs 300 --prefix TE_ESM2SI_3.1.1e-2.M.dropout2
steps.explanation: The README's TE and EL command for the Muscle cell line, using the ESM2SI_3.1 pretrained checkpoint. Change --cell_line to pc3 or HEK, and --label_type to rnaseq_log for the expression-level task. The README's --modelfile path does not match the repository tree: there is no Model folder under Scripts/UTRLM_downstream, and the checkpoint is at Model/Pretrained/ESM2SI_3.1_fiveSpeciesCao_6layers_16heads_128embedsize_4096batchToks_MLMLossMin.pkl. From Scripts/UTRLM_downstream, pass ../../Model/Pretrained/ESM2SI_3.1_fiveSpeciesCao_6layers_16heads_128embedsize_4096batchToks_MLMLossMin.pkl instead.
steps.source_locator: README.md: 2. For TE and EL task; GitHub tree listing, Model/Pretrained

outputs: Fine-tuning logs and a trained predictor checkpoint for the chosen cell line and label type. The README does not state the output paths; the prediction notebook MJ5_Predict_and_Extract_Attention_Embedding.ipynb reads such a checkpoint to produce predictions, embeddings and attention.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The checkpoint path in the README's TE command is ./Model/ESM2SI_3.1_... while the repository stores that file under Model/Pretrained/, so the path needs adjusting.
Data must be fetched by hand from Google Drive, with no checksum.

notes: Code and weights are GPL-3.0, so the README, LICENSE and requirements bytes are hashed and not stored. The paper was not readable openly (subscription in Europe PMC; the bioRxiv full-text page was rate-limited and the preprint is bioRxiv cc_no, so its bytes would not be stored), so only the abstract was used. The README's example pretraining flags (--heads 6 --embed_dim 16) contradict its own documented settings (16 heads, 128 embedding size); worth a human look before anyone follows that command.
